title: FedHPro: Federated Hyper-Prototype Learning via Gradient Matching
claim: Standard prototype aggregation leaves classes overlapping in hard domains; our approach yields tighter, better-separated class clusters and aligned prototypes.
layout: Domain images left, then Vanilla and Proposed scatter panels side by side
description: The crop shows the lower-right part of a wider figure, with the left side cut off. At the left are a camera icon and a 2x2 grid of SVHN street-number photos labeled 'SVHN'. A thick vertical gray bar separates them from two boxed t-SNE scatter plots. The first is labeled 'Vanilla' and the second 'Proposed'. Both plots show colored point clouds, one color per class, with a star marking each class prototype. In Vanilla the clusters overlap heavily and the stars sit in mixed regions. In Proposed the clusters are compact and clearly separated, and the stars sit near the cluster centers. Large bold serif labels sit under each panel. The eye goes first to the colorful scatter plots and the contrast between them.
caption: Illustration of heterogeneous FL with domain skew. The Vanilla column visualizes the feature distribution of a standard prototype-based FedProto [ref], showing failures in hard domains like SYN. In contrast, the Proposed column shows our approach achieves a larger inter-class distance and a smaller intra-class distance in such domains. Due to its simple aggregation, the prototypes in Vanilla (\protect\includegraphics[scale=0.18,valign=c]{./fig/4d8076.pdf}) fail to reliably align with class centers, whereas our Proposed (\protect\includegraphics[scale=0.18,valign=c]{./fig/c34a36.pdf}) yields better separability.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of distributed clients while protecting privacy. To enhance generalization capability in FL, prototype-based FL is in the spotlight, since shared global prototypes offer semantic anchors for aligning client-specific local prototypes. However, existing methods update global prototypes at the prototype-level via averaging local prototypes or refining global anchors, which often leads to semantic drift across clients and subsequently yields a misaligned global signal. To alleviate this issue, we introduce hyper-prototypes, defined by a set of learnable global class-wise prototypes to preserve underlying semantic knowledge across clients. The hyper-prototypes are optimized via gradient matching to align with class-relevant characteristics distilled directly from clients' real samples, rather than prototype-level descriptors. We further propose FedHPro, a Federated Hyper-Prototype Learning framework, to leverage hyper-prototypes to promote inter-class separability via mutual-contrastive learning with client-specific margin, while encouraging intra-class uniformity through a consistency penalty. Comprehensive experiments under diverse heterogeneous scenarios confirm that 1) hyper-prototypes produce a more semantically consistent global signal, and 2) FedHPro achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/mala-lab/FedHPro}{https://github.com/mala-lab/FedHPro}.
